108: function finishPackagedStartupValidation(error?: string): void {
109:   if (!packagedStartupValidation || startupCheckFinished) return;
110:   if (!error) {
111:     const snapshot = startupToolchainSnapshot;
112:     if (!startupRendererReady || !startupHostReady || !snapshot?.publicState.coreReady) return;
113:     if (!expectedPiVersion || hostManager?.getPiVersion() !== expectedPiVersion) {
114:       error = `Agent Host Pi version mismatch: expected ${expectedPiVersion ?? "unknown"}, got ${hostManager?.getPiVersion() ?? "unknown"}`;
115:     }
116:     if ((hostManager?.getToolchainAckRevision() ?? -1) < snapshot.revision) return;
117:     for (const capability of ["search.rg", "search.fd"] as const) {
118:       const candidates = snapshot.publicState.capabilities[capability]?.candidates ?? [];
119:       if (!candidates.some((candidate) => candidate.provider === "bundled" && candidate.health === "healthy")) return;
120:     }
121:   }
122: 
123:   startupCheckFinished = true;
124:   if (startupCheckTimer) clearTimeout(startupCheckTimer);
125:   try {
126:     const report = error
127:       ? { ok: false, error }
128:       : {
129:           ok: true,
130:           appVersion: app.getVersion(),
131:           piVersion: hostManager?.getPiVersion(),
132:           platformArch: `${process.platform}-${process.arch}`,
133:           revision: startupToolchainSnapshot?.revision,
134:           rendererReady: startupRendererReady,
135:           hostReady: startupHostReady,
136:           hostAckRevision: hostManager?.getToolchainAckRevision(),
137:           bundledSearch: ["search.rg", "search.fd"],
138:         };
139:     fs.mkdirSync(app.getPath("userData"), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
140:     fs.writeFileSync(
141:       path.join(app.getPath("userData"), "packaged-startup-check.json"),
142:       `${JSON.stringify(report, null, 2)}\n`,
143:       { encoding: "utf8", mode: 0o600 },
144:     );
145:   } catch (writeError) {
146:     error ??= writeError instanceof Error ? writeError.message : "Could not write packaged startup report";
147:   }
148:   isQuitting = true;
149:   updateManager?.stopAutomaticChecks();
150:   const exitCode = error ? 1 : 0;
151:   void (async () => {
152:     try {
153:       // The packaged probe exits immediately after startup. Let the utility
154:       // process release the packaged resources before Electron shuts down so
155:       // AppImage extraction mode can reap the temporary application cleanly.
156:       await hostManager?.stop();
157:     } catch (stopError) {
158:       appendMainLog(
159:         `packaged startup host shutdown failed: ${stopError instanceof Error ? stopError.message : String(stopError)}`,
160:       );
161:     } finally {
162:       for (const win of BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()) win.destroy();
163:       app.exit(exitCode);
164:     }
165:   })();
166: }

1: /**
2:  * Lightweight MessagePort RPC (no external framework).
3:  * Five message kinds: request / response / subscribe / unsubscribe / event.
4:  * Protocol spec: docs/rpc-protocol.md
5:  */
6: 
7: import type { ApiMethod, ApiParams, ApiResult, StreamTopic, Streams } from "./api";
8: import { RpcError, type RpcErrorShape } from "./types.ts";
9: import { ToolchainError } from "../shared/toolchains/errors.ts";

11: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
12: // Wire protocol
13: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
14: 
15: export type WireRequest = {
16:   kind: "request";
17:   id: string;
18:   method: string;
19:   params: unknown;
20: };
21: 
22: export type WireResponse = {
23:   kind: "response";
24:   id: string;
25:   ok: boolean;
26:   result?: unknown;
27:   error?: RpcErrorShape;
28: };
29: 
30: export type WireEvent = {
31:   kind: "event";
32:   topic: string;
33:   key: string;
34:   data: unknown;
35: };
36: 
37: export type WireSubscribe = {
38:   kind: "subscribe";
39:   id: string;
40:   topic: string;
41:   key: string;
42: };
43: 
44: export type WireUnsubscribe = {
45:   kind: "unsubscribe";
46:   id: string;
47:   topic: string;
48:   key: string;
49: };
50: 
51: export type WireMessage = WireRequest | WireResponse | WireEvent | WireSubscribe | WireUnsubscribe;
52: 
53: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
54: // Client (renderer / any consumer)
55: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
56: 
57: export interface PiRpc {
58:   call<M extends ApiMethod>(
59:     method: M,
60:     ...args: ApiParams<M> extends void ? [] | [void] : [ApiParams<M>]
61:   ): Promise<ApiResult<M>>;
62:   subscribe<T extends StreamTopic>(topic: T, key: string, on: (ev: Streams[T]) => void): () => void;
63:   close(): void;
64: }
65: 
66: type Pending = {
67:   resolve: (v: unknown) => void;
68:   reject: (e: Error) => void;
69:   timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;
70: };
71: 
72: type SubEntry = {
73:   topic: string;
74:   key: string;
75:   handler: (ev: unknown) => void;
76: };
77: 
78: let nextId = 0;
79: function makeId(): string {
80:   nextId += 1;
81:   return `r${nextId}_${Date.now().toString(36)}`;
82: }
83: 
84: export type RpcClientOptions = {
85:   callTimeoutMs?: number;
86: };
87: 
88: const DEFAULT_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000;
89: 
90: type RpcClientPort = {
91:   addEventListener(type: "message", listener: (event: MessageEvent) => void): void;
92:   addEventListener(type: "close", listener: () => void): void;
93:   removeEventListener(type: "message", listener: (event: MessageEvent) => void): void;
94:   removeEventListener(type: "close", listener: () => void): void;
95:   postMessage(message: unknown): void;
96:   start(): void;
97:   close(): void;
98: };
99: 
100: export function createRpcClient(port: RpcClientPort, options: RpcClientOptions = {}): PiRpc {
101:   const pending = new Map<string, Pending>();
102:   const subs = new Map<string, SubEntry>();
103:   const configuredTimeout = options.callTimeoutMs;
104:   const callTimeoutMs =
105:     typeof configuredTimeout === "number" && Number.isFinite(configuredTimeout) && configuredTimeout > 0
106:       ? configuredTimeout
107:       : DEFAULT_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS;
108: 
109:   const rejectPending = (shape: RpcErrorShape) => {
110:     for (const [, entry] of pending) {
111:       clearTimeout(entry.timer);
112:       entry.reject(new RpcError(shape));
113:     }
114:     pending.clear();
115:   };
116: 
117:   const onMessage = (ev: MessageEvent) => {
118:     const msg = ev.data as WireMessage;
119:     if (!msg || typeof msg !== "object") return;
120: 
121:     if (msg.kind === "response") {
122:       const p = pending.get(msg.id);
123:       if (!p) return;
124:       pending.delete(msg.id);
125:       clearTimeout(p.timer);
126:       if (msg.ok) p.resolve(msg.result);
127:       else {
128:         p.reject(new RpcError(msg.error ?? { code: "UNKNOWN", message: "Unknown RPC error" }));
129:       }
130:       return;
131:     }
132: 
133:     if (msg.kind === "event") {
134:       for (const sub of subs.values()) {
135:         if (sub.topic === msg.topic && (sub.key === "*" || sub.key === msg.key || msg.key === "*")) {
136:           try {
137:             sub.handler(msg.data);
138:           } catch {
139:             /* ignore subscriber errors */
140:           }
141:         }
142:       }
143:     }
144:   };
145: 
146:   const onClose = () => {
147:     rejectPending({ code: "CLOSED", message: "RPC port closed" });
148:     subs.clear();
149:   };
150: 
151:   port.addEventListener("message", onMessage);
152:   port.addEventListener("close", onClose);
153:   port.start();
154: 
155:   return {
156:     call(method, ...args) {
157:       const params = (args[0] ?? undefined) as unknown;
158:       const id = makeId();
159:       return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
160:         const timer = setTimeout(() => {
161:           if (!pending.delete(id)) return;
162:           reject(new RpcError({ code: "TIMEOUT", message: `RPC call timed out: ${String(method)}` }));
163:         }, callTimeoutMs);
164:         pending.set(id, {
165:           resolve: resolve as (v: unknown) => void,
166:           reject,
167:           timer,
168:         });
169:         const req: WireRequest = {
170:           kind: "request",
171:           id,
172:           method: method as string,
173:           params,
174:         };
175:         try {
176:           port.postMessage(req);
177:         } catch (err) {
178:           pending.delete(id);
179:           clearTimeout(timer);
180:           reject(err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(String(err)));
181:         }
182:       });
183:     },
184: 
185:     subscribe(topic, key, on) {
186:       const id = makeId();
187:       const msg: WireSubscribe = {
188:         kind: "subscribe",
189:         id,
190:         topic: topic as string,
191:         key,
192:       };
193:       port.postMessage(msg);
194:       subs.set(id, {
195:         topic: topic as string,
196:         key,
197:         handler: on as (ev: unknown) => void,
198:       });
199:       return () => {
200:         subs.delete(id);
201:         const unsub: WireUnsubscribe = {
202:           kind: "unsubscribe",
203:           id,
204:           topic: topic as string,
205:           key,
206:         };
207:         try {
208:           port.postMessage(unsub);
209:         } catch {
210:           /* ignore */
211:         }
212:       };
213:     },
214: 
215:     close() {
216:       port.removeEventListener("message", onMessage);
217:       port.removeEventListener("close", onClose);
218:       rejectPending({ code: "CLOSED", message: "RPC port closed" });
219:       subs.clear();
220:       try {
221:         port.close();
222:       } catch {
223:         /* ignore */
224:       }
225:     },
226:   };
227: }
228: 
229: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
230: // Server (agent-host)
231: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
232: 
233: export type RpcRequestContext = {
234:   setLease(key: string, release: () => void): void;
235:   releaseLease(key: string): boolean;
236: };
237: 
238: export type ApiHandler = {
239:   [M in ApiMethod]?: (params: ApiParams<M>, context: RpcRequestContext) => Promise<ApiResult<M>> | ApiResult<M>;
240: };
241: 
242: export type StreamSink = {
243:   topic: string;
244:   key: string;
245:   emit: (data: unknown) => void;
246: };

248: /**
249:  * Port shape that works in both:
250:  * - Renderer DOM MessagePort (addEventListener + MessageEvent.data)
251:  * - utilityProcess / Node worker_threads MessagePort (EventEmitter .on('message'))
252:  * - Electron MessagePortMain (.on('message', (e) => e.data))
253:  */
254: export type AnyMessagePort = {
255:   postMessage: (message: unknown, transfer?: unknown[]) => void;
256:   start?: () => void;
257:   close?: () => void;
258:   addEventListener?: (type: string, listener: (ev: { data: unknown }) => void) => void;
259:   removeEventListener?: (type: string, listener: (ev: { data: unknown }) => void) => void;
260:   on?: (event: string, listener: (...args: unknown[]) => void) => void;
261:   off?: (event: string, listener: (...args: unknown[]) => void) => void;
262:   removeListener?: (event: string, listener: (...args: unknown[]) => void) => void;
263: };
264: 
265: export interface RpcServer {
266:   handle(handlers: ApiHandler): void;
267:   emit<T extends StreamTopic>(topic: T, key: string, data: Streams[T]): void;
268:   attachPort(port: AnyMessagePort): void;
269:   detachPort(port: AnyMessagePort): void;
270: }
271: 
272: function extractMessageData(arg: unknown): unknown {
273:   // DOM MessageEvent / Electron MessagePortMain event: { data }
274:   if (arg && typeof arg === "object" && "data" in arg && !("kind" in arg)) {
275:     return (arg as { data: unknown }).data;
276:   }
277:   // Node worker_threads MessagePort: payload is the value itself
278:   return arg;
279: }
280: 
281: function listenPort(port: AnyMessagePort, onData: (data: unknown) => void): () => void {
282:   if (typeof port.addEventListener === "function") {
283:     const listener = (ev: { data: unknown }) => onData(ev.data);
284:     port.addEventListener("message", listener);
285:     port.start?.();
286:     return () => port.removeEventListener?.("message", listener);
287:   }
288: 
289:   if (typeof port.on === "function") {
290:     const listener = (...args: unknown[]) => {
291:       onData(extractMessageData(args[0]));
292:     };
293:     port.on("message", listener);
294:     port.start?.();
295:     return () => {
296:       port.off?.("message", listener);
297:       port.removeListener?.("message", listener);
298:     };
299:   }
300: 
301:   throw new Error("MessagePort has neither addEventListener nor on()");
302: }

304: export function createRpcServer(): RpcServer {
305:   const handlers = new Map<string, (params: unknown, context: RpcRequestContext) => Promise<unknown> | unknown>();
306:   const ports = new Set<AnyMessagePort>();
307:   /** port → subscription id → { topic, key } */
308:   const portSubs = new Map<AnyMessagePort, Map<string, { topic: string; key: string }>>();
309:   const portUnlisten = new Map<AnyMessagePort, () => void>();
310:   const portCloseUnlisten = new Map<AnyMessagePort, () => void>();
311:   const portLeases = new Map<AnyMessagePort, Map<string, () => void>>();
312: 
313:   function forgetPort(port: AnyMessagePort): void {
314:     ports.delete(port);
315:     portSubs.delete(port);
316:     const leases = portLeases.get(port);
317:     portLeases.delete(port);
318:     for (const release of leases?.values() ?? []) {
319:       try {
320:         release();
321:       } catch {
322:         /* isolate resource finalizers */
323:       }
324:     }
325:     portUnlisten.get(port)?.();
326:     portUnlisten.delete(port);
327:     portCloseUnlisten.get(port)?.();
328:     portCloseUnlisten.delete(port);
329:   }
330: 
331:   function requestContext(port: AnyMessagePort): RpcRequestContext {
332:     return {
333:       setLease(key, release) {
334:         if (!ports.has(port)) {
335:           release();
336:           return;
337:         }
338:         const leases = portLeases.get(port) ?? new Map<string, () => void>();
339:         const previous = leases.get(key);
340:         leases.set(key, release);
341:         portLeases.set(port, leases);
342:         if (previous && previous !== release) previous();
343:       },
344:       releaseLease(key) {
345:         const leases = portLeases.get(port);
346:         const release = leases?.get(key);
347:         if (!release) return false;
348:         leases?.delete(key);
349:         try {
350:           release();
351:         } catch {
352:           /* isolate explicit resource release */
353:         }
354:         return true;
355:       },
356:     };
357:   }
358: 
359:   function ensureSubs(port: AnyMessagePort): Map<string, { topic: string; key: string }> {
360:     let m = portSubs.get(port);
361:     if (!m) {
362:       m = new Map();
363:       portSubs.set(port, m);
364:     }
365:     return m;
366:   }
367: 
368:   async function onPortMessage(port: AnyMessagePort, raw: unknown) {
369:     const msg = raw as WireMessage;
370:     if (!msg || typeof msg !== "object") return;
371: 
372:     if (msg.kind === "subscribe") {
373:       ensureSubs(port).set(msg.id, { topic: msg.topic, key: msg.key });
374:       return;
375:     }
376:     if (msg.kind === "unsubscribe") {
377:       ensureSubs(port).delete(msg.id);
378:       return;
379:     }
380:     if (msg.kind !== "request") return;
381: 
382:     const handler = handlers.get(msg.method);
383: 
384:     let response: WireResponse;
385:     try {
386:       if (!handler) {
387:         throw new RpcError({

389:           message: `Unknown method: ${msg.method}`,

393:       response = { kind: "response", id: msg.id, ok: true, result };
394:     } catch (err) {
395:       const error: RpcErrorShape =
396:         err instanceof RpcError
397:           ? { code: err.code, message: err.message, detail: err.detail }

399:             ? {

401:                 message: err.message,
402:                 detail: { capability: err.capability, causeCode: err.causeCode },
403:               }
404:             : {
405:                 code: "INTERNAL",
406:                 message: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),

411:       port.postMessage(response);

415:         id: msg.id,
416:         ok: false,

214: type ModelsFileSnapshot = { raw: string | null; version: string };

216: function modelsContentVersion(raw: string | null): string {
217:   return raw === null ? "missing" : `sha256:${createHash("sha256").update(raw, "utf8").digest("hex")}`;

220: function readModelsFileSnapshot(): ModelsFileSnapshot {

227: function readModelsJsonSnapshot(): { config: Record<string, unknown>; version: string } {
228:   const snapshot = readModelsFileSnapshot();
229:   if (snapshot.raw === null) return { config: { providers: {} }, version: snapshot.version };
230:   try {
231:     return { config: JSON.parse(snapshot.raw) as Record<string, unknown>, version: snapshot.version };
232:   } catch (e) {
233:     // ISSUE-009: never silently return empty and allow overwrite of corrupt file
234:     throw new RpcError({
235:       code: "PARSE_ERROR",
236:       message: `Failed to parse models.json: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`,
237:     });

241: function modelsConfigConflict(expectedVersion: string, currentVersion: string): RpcError {
242:   return new RpcError({
243:     code: "CONFLICT",
244:     message: "models.json changed outside this editor; current edits were not saved",
245:     detail: { expectedVersion, currentVersion },
246:   });

249: function writeModelsJson(data: Record<string, unknown>, expectedVersion: string): string {
250:   const p = getModelsPath();
251:   mkdirSync(path.dirname(p), { recursive: true });
252:   const initial = readModelsFileSnapshot();
253:   if (initial.version !== expectedVersion) throw modelsConfigConflict(expectedVersion, initial.version);
254:   // ISSUE-009: atomic write via temp + rename; keep .bak of previous good file
255:   const tmp = `${p}.${process.pid}.tmp`;
256:   const bak = `${p}.bak`;
257:   const serialized = JSON.stringify(data, null, 2);
258:   writeFileSync(tmp, serialized, "utf8");
259:   try {
260:     const beforeCommit = readModelsFileSnapshot();
261:     if (beforeCommit.version !== expectedVersion) throw modelsConfigConflict(expectedVersion, beforeCommit.version);
262:     if (beforeCommit.raw !== null) {
263:       try {
264:         writeFileSync(bak, beforeCommit.raw, "utf8");
265:       } catch {
266:         /* ignore bak failure */
267:       }
268:     }
269:     renameSync(tmp, p);
270:   } catch (e) {
271:     try {
272:       unlinkSync(tmp);
273:     } catch {
274:       /* ignore */
275:     }
276:     throw e;
277:   }
278:   return modelsContentVersion(serialized);
279: }

318: function stripThinkingSuffix(modelRef: string): string {
319:   const trimmed = modelRef.trim();
320:   const colonIndex = trimmed.lastIndexOf(":");
321:   if (colonIndex === -1) return trimmed;
322:   const suffix = trimmed.substring(colonIndex + 1);
323:   return THINKING_SUFFIXES.has(suffix) ? trimmed.substring(0, colonIndex) : trimmed;

326: function filterByExactEnabledModels<T extends { id: string; provider: string }>(

331:   const refs = new Set(enabledModels.map(stripThinkingSuffix).filter(Boolean));
332:   const visible = available.filter((m) => refs.has(`${m.provider}/${m.id}`) || refs.has(m.id));
333:   return visible.length > 0 ? visible : available;

341:     .map((model) => ({ id: model.id, name: model.name, provider: model.provider }))
342:     .sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name) || a.provider.localeCompare(b.provider) || a.id.localeCompare(b.id));
343:   const normalized = [...new Set((enabledModels ?? []).map(stripThinkingSuffix).filter(Boolean))];

347: function normalizeEnabledModelsInput(value: unknown): string[] | undefined {
348:   if (value === null) return undefined;
349:   if (!Array.isArray(value) || value.length === 0 || value.length > 2000) {
350:     throw new RpcError({
351:       code: "BAD_REQUEST",
352:       message: "enabledModels must be null or a non-empty array with at most 2000 entries",
353:     });
354:   }
355: 
356:   const normalized: string[] = [];
357:   const seen = new Set<string>();
358:   for (const valueEntry of value) {
359:     if (typeof valueEntry !== "string") {
360:       throw new RpcError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "Every enabled model reference must be a string" });
361:     }
362:     const modelReference = stripThinkingSuffix(valueEntry);
363:     if (!modelReference || modelReference.length > 512) {
364:       throw new RpcError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "Invalid enabled model reference" });
365:     }
366:     if (!seen.has(modelReference)) {
367:       seen.add(modelReference);
368:       normalized.push(modelReference);
369:     }
370:   }
371:   return normalized;
372: }

421:   "Rules: match the language of the message; return only a short noun phrase " +

501:   if (existing?.isAlive()) {
502:     const name = existing.inner.sessionName;
503:     return typeof name === "string" && name.trim().length > 0;
504:   }
505:   try {
506:     const filePath = await resolveSessionPath(sessionId);
507:     if (!filePath) return false;
508:     const storedName = SessionManager.open(filePath, undefined).getSessionName();
509:     return typeof storedName === "string" && storedName.trim().length > 0;

515: function applyLiveSessionNameIfEmpty(sessionId: string, name: string): boolean | null {
516:   const existing = getRpcSession(sessionId);
517:   if (!existing?.isAlive()) return null;
518:   const currentName = existing.inner.sessionName;
519:   if (typeof currentName === "string" && currentName.trim().length > 0) return false;
520: 
521:   // Keep the check and write in the same synchronous turn. A manual rename
522:   // that ran first is observed above; one that runs later overwrites this
523:   // automatic value, so the manual choice always wins.
524:   existing.inner.setSessionName(name);
525:   return true;
526: }

528: export async function applySessionNameIfEmpty(sessionId: string, name: string): Promise<boolean> {
529:   const normalized = name.trim();
530:   if (!normalized) return false;
531: 
532:   const liveResult = applyLiveSessionNameIfEmpty(sessionId, normalized);
533:   if (liveResult !== null) return liveResult;
534: 
535:   const filePath = await resolveSessionPath(sessionId);
536:   if (!filePath) return false;
537: 
538:   // The session may have become live while its path was resolving.
539:   const liveResultAfterLookup = applyLiveSessionNameIfEmpty(sessionId, normalized);
540:   if (liveResultAfterLookup !== null) return liveResultAfterLookup;
541: 
542:   const manager = SessionManager.open(filePath, undefined);
543:   const storedName = manager.getSessionName();
544:   if (typeof storedName === "string" && storedName.trim().length > 0) return false;
545: 
546:   // SessionManager's read and append are synchronous, so another Renderer RPC
547:   // cannot interleave a manual rename between this final check and the write.
548:   manager.appendSessionInfo(normalized);
549:   invalidateSessionContent(filePath);
550:   return true;
551: }

553: async function resolveTitleSessionTarget(
554:   sessionId: string,
555: ): Promise<{ cwd: string; services?: TitleModelServices } | null> {
556:   const existing = getRpcSession(sessionId);
557:   if (existing?.isAlive()) {
558:     const dir = validateExistingDirectory(existing.cwd);
559:     if (!dir.ok) return null;
560:     return {
561:       cwd: dir.path,
562:       services: {
563:         modelRuntime: existing.inner.modelRuntime as unknown as TitleSessionServices["modelRuntime"],
564:         settingsManager: existing.inner.settingsManager,
565:       },
566:     };
567:   }
568: 
569:   const filePath = await resolveSessionPath(sessionId);
570:   if (!filePath) return null;
571:   const cwd = SessionManager.open(filePath, undefined).getHeader()?.cwd;
572:   const dir = validateExistingDirectory(cwd);
573:   return dir.ok ? { cwd: dir.path } : null;
574: }

576: type DirectoryValidation = { ok: true; path: string; canonicalPath: string } | { ok: false; error: string };
577: 
578: function validateExistingDirectory(candidate: unknown): DirectoryValidation {
579:   if (typeof candidate !== "string" || !candidate) return { ok: false, error: "Directory does not exist" };
580:   try {
581:     const realpath = realpathSync.native ?? realpathSync;
582:     const canonicalPath = realpath(candidate);
583:     if (!statSync(canonicalPath).isDirectory()) return { ok: false, error: "Not a directory" };
584:     return { ok: true, path: candidate, canonicalPath };
585:   } catch {
586:     return { ok: false, error: "Directory does not exist" };
587:   }
588: }

590: function canonicalPathForComparison(candidate: string): string {
591:   const resolved = path.resolve(candidate);
592:   let canonical = resolved;
593:   try {
594:     const realpath = realpathSync.native ?? realpathSync;
595:     canonical = realpath(resolved);
596:   } catch {
597:     // Historical session cwd values can refer to directories that no longer exist.
598:   }
599:   return process.platform === "win32" ? canonical.toLowerCase() : canonical;
600: }

604: async function resolveAvailableModels(
605:   modelRuntime: ModelRuntime,
606:   signal?: AbortSignal,
607: ): Promise<{ models: AvailableModel[]; warnings: ModelCatalogWarning[] }> {
608:   const snapshot = [...modelRuntime.getAvailableSnapshot()];
609:   const snapshotByProvider = new Map<string, AvailableModel[]>();
610:   for (const model of snapshot) {
611:     const models = snapshotByProvider.get(model.provider) ?? [];
612:     models.push(model);
613:     snapshotByProvider.set(model.provider, models);
614:   }
615: 
616:   const results = await Promise.all(
617:     [...modelRuntime.getProviders()]
618:       .sort((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id))
619:       .map(async (provider) => {
620:         try {
621:           const models = [...(await modelRuntime.getAvailable(provider.id, { signal }))];
622:           return { models, warning: undefined };
623:         } catch (error) {
624:           if (signal?.aborted) throw signal.reason ?? error;
625:           return {
626:             models: snapshotByProvider.get(provider.id) ?? [],
627:             warning: {
628:               provider: provider.id,
629:               code: "PROVIDER_AVAILABILITY_FAILED" as const,
630:               message: `Unable to check ${provider.id} model availability; the last known state remains available.`,
631:             },
632:           };
633:         }
634:       }),
635:   );
636:   signal?.throwIfAborted();
637:   return {
638:     models: results.flatMap((result) => result.models),
639:     warnings: results.flatMap((result) => (result.warning ? [result.warning] : [])),
640:   };
641: }

643: export async function projectModelsList(

649:   const availability = options.cachedOnly

651:     : await resolveAvailableModels(modelRuntime, options.signal);
652:   const available = availability.models;
653:   const enabledModels = settings.getEnabledModels();
654:   const visible = filterByExactEnabledModels(available, enabledModels);
655:   const models = visible
656:     .map((model) => ({ id: model.id, name: model.name, provider: model.provider }))
657:     .sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name) || a.provider.localeCompare(b.provider));
658: 
659:   const nameMap: Record<string, string> = {};
660:   const thinkingLevels: Record<string, string[]> = {};
661:   const thinkingLevelMaps: Record<string, Record<string, string | null>> = {};
662:   for (const model of visible) {
663:     const key = `${model.provider}:${model.id}`;
664:     nameMap[key] = model.name;
665:     thinkingLevels[key] = getSupportedThinkingLevels(model);
666:     if (model.thinkingLevelMap) thinkingLevelMaps[key] = model.thinkingLevelMap;

669:   let defaultModel: { provider: string; modelId: string } | null = null;
670:   const provider = settings.getDefaultProvider();
671:   const modelId = settings.getDefaultModel();
672:   if (provider && modelId && visible.some((model) => model.provider === provider && model.id === modelId)) {
673:     defaultModel = { provider, modelId };

676:   return {
677:     models,
678:     defaultModel,
679:     thinkingLevels,
680:     thinkingLevelMaps,
681:     nameMap,
682:     catalog: availability.warnings.length
683:       ? { ...catalog, warnings: [...catalog.warnings, ...availability.warnings] }
684:       : catalog,

27:   constructor(value: ParentRpcError) {
28:     const recovery = value.recovery
29:       ? ` Recovery: ${value.recovery.remediation}; reason=${value.recovery.reason}; retryable=${value.recovery.retryable}.`
30:       : "";
31:     super(value.code ? `${value.code}: ${value.message}.${recovery}` : value.message);
32:     this.name = "MainProcessRpcError";
33:     this.code = value.code;
34:     this.retryable = value.retryable === true;
35:     this.recovery = value.recovery ? structuredClone(value.recovery) : undefined;
36:     this.details = value.details ? structuredClone(value.details) : undefined;
37:   }
38: }
39: 
40: function installListener(): void {
41:   if (installed || !process.parentPort) return;
42:   installed = true;
43:   process.parentPort.on("message", (event) => {
44:     const message = event.data as ParentRpcResult;
45:     if (message?.type !== "host-rpc-result") return;
46:     const request = pending.get(message.id);
47:     if (!request) return;
48:     pending.delete(message.id);
49:     clearTimeout(request.timer);
50:     if (message.ok) request.resolve(message.result);
51:     else request.reject(new MainProcessRpcError(message.error ?? { message: "Main process request failed" }));
52:   });
53: }
54: 
55: export function callMain<T>(method: string, params?: unknown, timeoutMs = 10_000): Promise<T> {
56:   installListener();
57:   const port = process.parentPort;
58:   if (!port) return Promise.reject(new Error("Main process channel is unavailable"));
59:   const id = randomUUID();
60:   return new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
61:     const timer = setTimeout(() => {
62:       pending.delete(id);
63:       reject(new Error(`Main process request timed out: ${method}`));
64:     }, timeoutMs);
65:     pending.set(id, { resolve: resolve as (value: unknown) => void, reject, timer });
66:     port.postMessage({ type: "host-rpc", id, method, params });
67:   });
68: }

---
type: architecture
title: IPC and Type Contracts
description: The typed IPC/RPC layer that connects the Electron Main process, the Agent Host utility process, and the sandboxed renderer — wire protocol, contracts, preload bridge, reverse RPC, and sender-trust gating.
tags: [ipc, rpc, contracts, preload, messageport, architecture]
---

# IPC and Type Contracts

Pi Agent Desktop has no internal HTTP/TCP control plane. Every cross-process interaction is carried over Electron `MessagePort` objects or `ipcMain`/`ipcRenderer` channels, and every payload type is declared in TypeScript contracts under `src/contract/`. The surfaces are:

1. **Renderer ↔ Agent Host**: a typed request/response + stream RPC protocol over a transferred `MessagePort` (`src/contract/rpc.ts`, `src/contract/api.ts`).
2. **Renderer ↔ Main**: the `piBridge` preload surface, one `ipcRenderer.invoke`/`send` channel per operation, registered in `src/main/ipc.ts`.
3. **Agent Host → Main**: a reverse one-shot RPC over `process.parentPort` for browser requests, toolchain resolution, managed-process registration, and channel secrets (`src/agent-host/parent-rpc.ts`).

## Host MessagePort RPC protocol

`src/contract/rpc.ts` defines five wire messages: `request`, `response`, `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, and `event` (`WireMessage`, `src/contract/rpc.ts:15-51`). A request carries an `id`, a `method` name, and `params`; the response echoes the `id` with `ok` plus either a `result` or an error shape. There is no framing beyond a single `postMessage` per message, and the port type is duck-typed so the same server code works with DOM `MessagePort`, Node `worker_threads`, and Electron `MessagePortMain` (`AnyMessagePort`, `src/contract/rpc.ts:254-263`).

The client side (`createRpcClient`, `src/contract/rpc.ts:100-227`) keeps a map of in-flight requests, defaults calls to a 120 s timeout (`DEFAULT_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS`, `src/contract/rpc.ts:88`), and rejects every pending call with `CLOSED` when the port closes. Subscriptions are keyed by `(topic, key)`, and event delivery matches when either side uses the `"*"` wildcard (`src/contract/rpc.ts:133-144`).

The server side (`createRpcServer`, `src/contract/rpc.ts:304-507`) dispatches to a handler map, tracks per-port subscriptions, and releases per-port resources when a port is detached or closes. The `RpcRequestContext` given to every handler exposes lease semantics: `setLease(key, release)` installs (and replaces) a release callback keyed by lease name, and `releaseLease(key)` runs and removes it; all outstanding leases for a port are released when the port is forgotten (`src/contract/rpc.ts:331-357`). Handlers that own long-lived resources use leases — for example `files.watchStart` registers a `files.watch:<path>` lease that `files.watchStop` or port disconnect releases (`src/agent-host/handlers.ts:1899-1916`).

Errors cross the wire as `{ code, message, detail }`. The server serializes `RpcError` verbatim, converts `ToolchainError` to its code/capability/causeCode detail, and maps anything else to `INTERNAL`; if the response itself cannot be serialized it sends `SERIALIZATION_FAILED` and, on further failure, drops the port (`src/contract/rpc.ts:384-429`).

## The Api and Streams contracts

`src/contract/api.ts` is the single source of truth for the request/response surface. The `Api` interface declares `params` and `result` for every method grouped by domain: sessions (`sessions.*`), agent lifecycle (`agent.*`), worktrees and git, files, models and auth, skills/plugins, channels, managed processes (`processes.*`), and small `system.*` helpers (`Api`, `src/contract/api.ts:57-392`). The `Streams` interface declares the server-push topics, including `agent.events`, `sessions.changed`, `files.changed`, `channels.*`, and `processes.*` (`Streams`, `src/contract/api.ts:395-420`). Domain types shared with the Host and the renderer live in `src/contract/types.ts` (e.g. `RpcError` and `RpcErrorShape`, `src/contract/types.ts:224-239`).

Contract coverage is machine-checked, not advisory. `scripts/check-contract-coverage.mjs` statically parses `api.ts`, `handlers.ts`, `desktop.ts`, `preload.ts`, `ipc.ts`, `browser.ts`, and `browser-service.ts` and fails unless every `Api` method has a server handler, every `Streams` topic is emitted, every `PiBridge` method is implemented, every IPC invoke/send channel is registered, and the browser Host method set matches both the `BrowserHostRpc` interface and the `dispatchHostRequest` cases (`analyzeContractCoverage`, `scripts/check-contract-coverage.mjs:229-290`). It runs inside the `verify` gate.

## The preload bridge and Host port transfer

The renderer is sandboxed and gets a single `piBridge` object via `contextBridge` (`contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld("piBridge", bridge)`, `src/preload/preload.ts:187`). The full shape is the `PiBridge` interface in `src/contract/desktop.ts:131-226`. The bridge is deliberately narrow: platform/version, update control, Host status and toolchain state, file/project operations, UI state, browser control, and a fixed set of `on*` event subscriptions. Main-to-renderer events that fire before React subscribes are buffered one generation each by `EarlyEventReplay` (deep links and menu commands, `src/preload/preload.ts:29-53`).

The Host `MessagePort` is never exposed through `contextBridge` (a Promise-resolved port silently breaks). Instead the preload listens for the `desktop:host-port` IPC event and forwards the transferred port to the page with `window.postMessage(..., "*", [port])` on the channel `"pi-desktop-host-port"` (`src/preload/preload.ts:16-26`). The renderer retrieves it in `requestHostPort()` (`src/renderer/lib/api-client.ts:43-72`), then `ensureRpc()` waits for Host `ready` (30 s), creates the RPC client, and verifies the connection with a `host.ping` round-trip before use (`src/renderer/lib/api-client.ts:118-141`).

Preload hardening lives in two small policy modules. `isTrustedPreloadLocation` only enables the port-forwarding bridge for `app://bundle` or dev-server `localhost:5173` pages (`src/preload/preload-location-policy.ts:1-11`). `selectTransferredHostPort` validates that exactly one object with working `postMessage`/`start`/`close` methods is transferred, and `isValidDeepLinkSessionMessage` constrains deep-link session ids to the UUID shape (`src/preload/preload-message-policy.ts:7-24`).

## Desktop IPC and sender trust

`src/main/ipc.ts` registers every `desktop:*` channel. `installDesktopIpc` wraps each registration in `trustedHandle` (invoke) or `trustedOn` (send), which first calls `assertTrustedSender` (`src/main/ipc.ts:83-104`). Trust means the sender's `webContents` is the main window's `webContents` and the `senderFrame` is its `mainFrame` — subframes and other `WebContents` are rejected (`isTrustedDesktopIpcSender`, `src/main/ipc.ts` / `src/main/ipc-trust.ts:13-19`). This is the boundary that keeps untrusted web content in the built-in Browser from reaching desktop capabilities.

The renderer asks for the Host port over `desktop:connect-host`; Main answers by creating a `MessageChannelMain` and transferring one side to the Host via `attachRendererPort` (`src/main/ipc.ts:177-182`, `HostManager.createRendererChannel`, `src/main/host-manager.ts:162-166`). Desktop operations that need Host services in the middle (e.g. HTML preview asset loads) call the Host through `HostManager.call`, a one-shot RPC over a fresh channel (`src/main/host-manager.ts:169-202`).

## Reverse RPC: Agent Host → Main

The Host reaches Main with `callMain(method, params, timeoutMs)` (`src/agent-host/parent-rpc.ts:55-68`), which posts `{ type: "host-rpc", id, method, params }` on `process.parentPort` and matches the async reply against `host-rpc-result`. `HostManager` receives these in its message handler and dispatches them to the request handler configured by `main.ts`: `channelSecrets.*` hits the credential vault, `toolchain.*` hits the toolchain manager, `managedProcesses.*` hits the reaper (with owner-generation checks on Windows), and `browser.*` hits `BrowserService.handleHostRequest` (`src/main/main.ts:590-685`). Browser host requests are validated against the `BrowserHostRpc` contract and the `BROWSER_HOST_METHODS` set before dispatch (`src/contract/browser.ts:728,961-969`).

## Error taxonomy

Handlers and bridges surface a small set of structured errors:

- `RpcError` — `{ code, message, detail? }`, thrown by Host handlers for business failures (`FORBIDDEN`, `NOT_FOUND`, `CONFLICT`, `BAD_REQUEST`, `PARSE_ERROR`, `STALE_CURSOR`, `RESULT_TOO_LARGE`, `INTERNAL`) (`src/contract/types.ts:230-239`).
- `ToolchainError` — adds `capability` and `causeCode` for developer-tool failures (`src/shared/toolchains/errors.ts:12-26`).
- `BrowserError` — carries `retryable`, a `recovery` reason/remediation, and `toJSON()` for the structured wire form; the recovery table classifies each code (`src/main/browser/browser-error.ts:3-36,46-110`).
- `MainProcessRpcError` — the Host-side view of a failed Main/browser request, preserving `code`/`retryable`/`recovery` (`src/agent-host/parent-rpc.ts:21-38`).

Desktop IPC handlers translate these into single-line `CODE: message` strings (e.g. `browserHandler` rethrows `BrowserError` as `${code}: ${message}`) so the renderer never receives raw objects of unknown shape (`src/main/ipc.ts:111-124`).

## Related pages

- [Architecture Overview](/openwiki/architecture/overview.md)
- [Security and Trust Model](/openwiki/security/security-model.md)
- [Agent Host: Runtime, Sessions, Models, Extensions](/openwiki/systems/agent-host.md)
- [Change Guides](/openwiki/development/change-guides.md)

parts.text:
I have enough for the overview. Let me write it. Key facts:

- Three-process Electron architecture: Main, Agent Host (utilityProcess), Renderer (React 19 + Vite), plus Main-owned WebContentsView browser and managed project processes.
- Main responsibilities: window lifecycle, menus, tray/badge, deep link, protocol, Host supervision, browser service, toolchains, updates. No business logic (comment in main.ts).
- Agent Host: utilityProcess forked from out/main/agent-host.mjs with serviceName "pi-agent-host", env PI_AGENT_HOST=1, PI_DESKTOP_USER_DATA, PI_DESKTOP_VERSION. It runs pi-coding-agent in-process, serves Api/Streams over MessagePort. Fallback to standalone mode if no parentPort.
- Host supervision: HostManager spawn, statuses starting/ready/crashed/stopped; restart budget MAX_RESTARTS=2 within CRASH_WINDOW_MS=30s; ping interval 15s timeout 10s heartbeat; before-restart handler (reap managed processes); snapshot init/changed delivery (toolchain, browser) with ack; managed-process owner identity.
- Renderer: sandbox: true, contextIsolation: true, nodeIntegration: false, webSecurity: true; preload; strict CSP (app protocol); React UI; talks to Host via MessagePort and to Main via piBridge.
- Browser: main-owned WebContentsView, no app preload/Node.
- Data flow: Host <-> ~/.pi/agent/.
- Startup sequence in main.ts whenReady.
- No internal TCP for control plane; managed services may listen on loopback.

Also renderer entry resolution (resolveRendererEntry) - Vite dev server, built index, app://bundle.

The startup sequence:
1. registerAppProtocol (before ready)
2. single instance lock
3. whenReady: 
   - packaged cleanup fault validation path
   - Windows helper resolution on win32 x64
   - reaper initialize
   - credential vault, BrowserService
   - update manager
   - toolchain manager + subscribe (sends toolchains:state to windows, snapshot to host)
   - handleAppProtocol
   - installDesktopIpc, installAppMenu, createTray, theme
   - HostManager start
   - createWindow, toolchainManager.initialize, updateManager.startAutomaticChecks

Let me write the overview page. I'll cover:
- process model & ownership
- startup sequence
- Host supervision lifecycle (liveness, restart budget)
- snapshot/ack pipeline
- data & control flows (renderer→host port, renderer→main bridge, host→main reverse, browser→main)
- persistence location
- security posture pointer

Let me write concise but substantive.

input.content:
--- type: architecture title: Architecture Overview description: The three-process Electron architecture of Pi Agent Desktop — Electron Main, the Agent Host utilityProcess, and the sandboxed React renderer — with a Main-owned WebContentsView browser, process ownership boundaries, and the primary data and control flows between them. tags: [architecture, electron, processes, ownership, agent-host, main] --- # Architecture Overview Pi Agent Desktop is an Electron desktop workspace that embeds the Pi Coding Agent runtime. It uses a three-process architecture to isolate privileged desktop capabilities (Main), the Agent runtime (Agent Host), and the UI (Renderer), with a fourth Main-owned surface for remote web pages (Browser). ```mermaid flowchart LR Main["Electron Main
window · tray · protocol · Host supervision"] Host["Agent Host / utilityProcess
Pi Agent · sessions · files · configuration"] UI["Renderer
React 19 · Vite"] Browser["Main-owned WebContentsView
remote pages · profiles · network policy"] Processes["managed project processes
dev server · watcher · mock API"] Data["~/.pi/agent/
sessions · models · configuration"] Main --> Host Main --> UI Main --> Browser Host -->|"MessagePort RPC"| UI Host -->|"POSIX group / Windows Job helper"| Processes Host -.->|"host-rpc (parentPort)"| Main Main -.->|"crash reaper"| Processes Browser -->|"separately authorized localhost access"| Processes Host <--> Data ``` ## Process ownership - **Electron Main** (`src/main/main.ts`) owns everything desktop: the window, menu, tray and Dock/taskbar badges, custom `app://` protocol, deep links, software updates, the Browser service, the developer-toolchain manager, the credential vault, and supervision of the Agent Host. Its header comment states the boundary explicitly: "No business logic" (`src/main/main.ts:1-5`). Business behavior lives in the Host. - **Agent Host** (`src/agent-host/index.ts`) is a `utilityProcess` forked by `HostManager` from the built `agent-host.mjs` entry with `serviceName: "pi-agent-host"` and an environment that sets `PI_AGENT_HOST=1`, `PI_DESKTOP_USER_DATA`, and `PI_DESKTOP_VERSION` (`src/main/host-manager.ts:230-236`). It runs the `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` runtime in-process and implements the desktop RPC contract (`registerHandlers`), file watching, session indexing, channels, and managed processes. It also installs a `toolchain-git` runner override and a session watcher before serving (`src/agent-host/index.ts:19-22`). - **Renderer** (`src/renderer/main.tsx`, `src/renderer/App.tsx`) is a React 19 app built with Vite. It loads in a `BrowserWindow` with `sandbox: true`, `contextIsolation: true`, `nodeIntegration: false`, and `webSecurity: true`, plus a strict Content Security Policy served from the `app://` protocol (`src/main/window.ts:48-54`, `src/main/protocol.ts:11-25`). It communicates only through the preload `piBridge` and the transferred Host `MessagePort`. - **Browser** is a set of `WebContentsView` instances created by Main. Remote pages load in sandboxed sessions without the app preload, Node.js, or the main Renderer bridge (`src/main/browser/browser-service.ts`, `browser-tab-manager.ts`). - **Managed project processes** are children spawned by the Agent Host (POSIX process groups or, on Windows x64, a Job Object via the Rust helper), reaped by a Main-process crash reaper (`src/main/managed-process/reaper.ts`). ## Startup sequence `startMainProcess` (`src/main/main.ts:283`) registers the `app://` protocol before `ready`, acquires the single-instance lock (second instances forward a deep link instead), and then runs the `whenReady` pipeline: 1. Optional packaged validation probes (`--validate-packaged-startup` / `--validate-packaged-cleanup-fault`) exit early with a JSON report. 2. On Windows x64 the integrity-verified managed-process helper is resolved. 3. The managed-process reaper is initialized from its journal. 4. The credential vault, `BrowserService`, update manager, and `ToolchainManager` are constructed; toolchain state subscriptions broadcast `toolchains:state` to every window and push snapshots to the Host (`src/main/main.ts:484-544`). 5. Desktop IPC is installed, the menu and tray are created, and the persisted theme is applied. 6. `HostManager` spawns the Agent Host, the main window is created, the toolchain scan starts, and automatic update checks begin (`src/main/main.ts:751-755`). ## Host supervision lifecycle `HostManager` (`src/main/host-manager.ts`) is the supervisor. It exposes a status machine `starting | ready | crashed | stopped` (`src/main/host-manager.ts:22`) and drives restart policy: - On `ready`, it delivers the current **toolchain snapshot** and **browser capability snapshot** to the Host (`toolchain:init` / `browser:init`) and the managed-process owner identity (`managed-process-owner:init`); the Host acknowledges each with a revision (`src/main/host-manager.ts:265-297`). - Liveness is a 15 s ping / 10 s timeout heartbeat; a missed heartbeat kills the child, which triggers the crash path (`src/main/host-manager.ts:386-416`). - Restarts are budgeted: at most `MAX_RESTARTS = 2` within a `CRASH_WINDOW_MS = 30_000` window, then the status becomes `crashed` (`src/main/host-manager.ts:368-384`). Before restart, the `beforeRestartHandler` reaps managed processes and blocks restart if cleanup is not confirmed (`src/main/main.ts:579-587`). - Every `ready` Host must acknowledge both policy snapshots and the owner identity itself; acknowledgements from a previous Host are not transferable (`src/main/host-manager.ts:209-216`). - On exit, the Host posts `shutdown` and the manager force-kills after 10 s if it does not exit (`src/main/host-manager.ts:112-137`). The Host treats uncaught exceptions and unhandled rejections as fatal: it logs and `process.exit(1)` so the supervisor restarts it (`src/agent-host/index.ts:113-122`). ## Data and control flows - **Renderer → Host**: the sandboxed renderer receives a transferred `MessagePort` (`pi-desktop-host-port`) and issues typed `Api` calls and `Streams` subscriptions over the RPC protocol (`src/renderer/lib/api-client.ts:43-72`; protocol in `src/contract/rpc.ts`). - **Renderer → Main**: `piBridge` invoke/send channels cover desktop-only operations (updates, file dialogs, browser control, UI state) (`src/preload/preload.ts:55-185`). - **Host → Main**: one-shot reverse RPC over `process.parentPort` (`callMain`, `src/agent-host/parent-rpc.ts:55-68`) reaches Main for channel secrets, toolchain resolution, managed-process registration, and browser host requests (`src/main/main.ts:590-685`). - **Host → Renderer**: server-push `Streams` events (agent progress, session changes, files, channels, processes) delivered over the same MessagePort; Main also pushes `host:status`, `toolchains:state`, `update:state`, and `browser:event` via `webContents.send`. - **Persistence**: the Host reads and writes session and configuration data under the Pi agent directory (`~/.pi/agent/` by default via `getAgentDir`), sharing it with the Pi CLI without migration (`src/agent-host/handlers.ts:1512-1513`, `README.en.md`). ## Security posture (summary) The renderer runs fully sandboxed with a strict CSP; the preload exposes only `piBridge`; every desktop IPC handler validates the sender; and the Host's file access is constrained by an allowed-roots policy. Details are covered in [Security and Trust Model](/openwiki/security/security-model.md). Notably, the app does not open a TCP port for its UI or control plane; only user-started managed project services may listen on loopback. ## Related pages - [IPC and Type Contracts](/openwiki/architecture/ipc-and-contracts.md) - [Agent Host: Runtime, Sessions, Models, Extensions](/openwiki/systems/agent-host.md) - [Security and Trust Model](/openwiki/security/security-model.md) - [Desktop Lifecycle](/openwiki/operations/desktop-lifecycle.md) - [Quickstart](/openwiki/quickstart.md)

claims.statement: The Electron Main process owns window, menu, tray, protocol, deep links, updates, the Browser service, toolchains, credentials, and Agent Host supervision, and deliberately contains no business logic.
The Agent Host runs as a utilityProcess forked from the built agent-host.mjs with serviceName 'pi-agent-host' and an environment that sets PI_AGENT_HOST, PI_DESKTOP_USER_DATA, and PI_DESKTOP_VERSION.
The Agent Host runs the pi-coding-agent runtime in-process, registers the desktop RPC handlers, installs a toolchain Git runner override, and starts a session watcher before serving.
The main window loads the renderer with sandbox, contextIsolation, and webSecurity enabled and no nodeIntegration, and the app:// protocol serves it with a strict Content Security Policy.

HostManager exposes a starting/ready/crashed/stopped status machine and delivers toolchain and browser capability snapshots plus managed-process owner identity to each newly ready Host, requiring per-Host acknowledgements.
Host liveness is enforced by a 15 s ping interval with a 10 s heartbeat timeout; a missed heartbeat kills the Host and triggers the crash path.
Host restarts are budgeted to at most 2 attempts within a 30 s window before the status becomes crashed, and restart is blocked unless managed-process cleanup is confirmed.
On shutdown the Host is asked to exit gracefully and is force-killed after 10 s if it does not.
The Agent Host treats uncaught exceptions and unhandled rejections as fatal, logging and exiting so the Main supervisor restarts it.
The renderer receives the Host MessagePort through a window.postMessage transfer on channel 'pi-desktop-host-port' and issues typed RPC calls over it.
The Agent Host reaches Main with one-shot host-rpc calls over process.parentPort, dispatched to the credential vault, toolchain manager, managed-process reaper, or BrowserService.

Startup acquires a single-instance lock, then in whenReady constructs the reaper, vault, browser, updater, and toolchain manager, starts the Host, creates the window, and begins toolchain scanning and automatic update checks.
Session and configuration data is read from the Pi agent directory (~/.pi/agent/ by default), shared with the Pi CLI without migration.
The app does not expose an internal TCP control plane; only user-started managed project services may listen on loopback.

# Pi Agent Desktop v2 — pure Electron (no Next sidecar, no bundled Node)
appId: app.dlyzzt.pi-agent-desktop
productName: Pi Agent Desktop
copyright: Copyright © DLYZZT

directories:
  output: dist
  buildResources: build

files:
  - out/**/*
  - package.json
  - LICENSE
  - build/icon.png

  - "!node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/examples/**/*"
  # Pi injects these package-relative paths into the agent system prompt when
  # users ask it to author extensions, packages, SDK integrations, or TUI UI.
  # Restore them after the broad Markdown/TypeScript production exclusions.
  # Explicit FileSets bypass electron-builder's production-dependency cleanup,
  # which otherwise drops package READMEs, examples, and declaration files.
  - from: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
    to: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
    filter:
      - README.md
      - "docs/**/*"
      - "examples/**/*"
      # Public declarations let the agent inspect exact APIs when the prose and
      # examples do not cover a newly added or advanced extension capability.
      - "dist/**/*.d.ts"
  - from: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist
    to: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist
    filter:
      - "**/*.d.ts"
  # Keep telemetry as an exact root dependency so electron-builder has one
  # runtime source. Restore only authoring files excluded from the default
  # dependency walk; copying JS here would race the ASAR dependency copier.
  - from: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-telemetry
    to: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-telemetry
    filter:
      - README.md
      - "dist/**/*.d.ts"
  # electron-builder deduplicates these transitive packages to the app root.
  # Re-adding declaration-only nested directories would shadow the healthy
  # root package under Node's ESM resolver, so package metadata and runtime JS
  # must travel with the authoring declarations.
  - from: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai
    to: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai
    filter:
      - package.json
      - "dist/**/*.js"
      - "dist/**/*.json"
      - "dist/**/*.d.ts"
  - from: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui

    filter:

  - from: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-client

    filter:

      - "dist/**/*.js"

  - from: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-protocol
    to: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-protocol
    filter:

  - from: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-telemetry
    to: node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-telemetry

asar: true

# Signed runtime catalogs plus the current target's small core search tools.

  artifactName: Pi-Agent-Desktop-Unsigned-Beta-Setup-${version}.${ext}

        - x64
  category: Development
  artifactName: Pi-Agent-Desktop-${version}-${arch}.${ext}
  synopsis: Local desktop UI for the pi coding agent

protocols:
  - name: Pi Agent Desktop
    schemes:
      - pi-agent-desktop

publish:
  provider: github
  owner: DLYZZT
  repo: pi-desktop
  releaseType: draft

434:                 `${source} (${String(version)}) does not match package.json (${packageJson.version})`,
435:               );
436:             }
437:           }
438: 
439:           if (process.env.GITHUB_REF_NAME !== expectedTag) {

441:               `Release tag ${process.env.GITHUB_REF_NAME} must exactly match ${expectedTag}`,

443:           }

547:               const entryPath = path.join(directory, entry.name);
548:               if (entry.isDirectory()) {
549:                 findUpdateConfigs(entryPath, matches);

551:                 entry.isFile() &&

574:               (value.startsWith('"') && value.endsWith('"')) ||
575:               (value.startsWith("'") && value.endsWith("'"))

624:             for (const [label, pattern] of forbidden) {

637:             );

798:                 )

804:           }

808:               new RegExp(`^\\s*${key}\\s*:\\s*([^#\\r\\n]+)`, "mi"),

display.text:
name: Build desktop apps

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    tags:
      - "v*"
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: desktop-build-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ !startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') }}

jobs:
  test-platforms:
    name: Tests (${{ matrix.name }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: Linux x64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04
            timeout_minutes: 25
          - name: macOS arm64
            runner: macos-15
            timeout_minutes: 25
          - name: macOS x64
            runner: macos-15-intel
            timeout_minutes: 25
          - name: Windows x64
            runner: windows-2025
            timeout_minutes: 45
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.timeout_minutes }}
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install pinned Rust toolchain (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: rustup toolchain install 1.96.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --profile minimal --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc

      - name: Install pinned Windows cross toolchain (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install 1.96.1 --profile minimal --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          cargo install cargo-xwin --locked --version 0.23.1
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --no-install-recommends clang-18 lld-18 llvm-18

      - name: Compile-check Windows helper with cargo-xwin (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: npm run build:windows-helper

      - name: Install pinned Rust supply-chain gates (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          cargo install cargo-audit --locked --version 0.22.2
          cargo install cargo-deny --locked --version 0.20.2

      - name: Install Electron binary (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: npx install-electron --no

      - name: Validate Windows managed process helper
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true
          python -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check --no-input Flask==3.1.0 fastapi==0.128.0 uvicorn==0.40.0
          cargo fmt --manifest-path native/windows-managed-process-helper/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
          cargo clippy --manifest-path native/windows-managed-process-helper/Cargo.toml --locked --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc -- -D warnings
          cargo test --manifest-path native/windows-managed-process-helper/Cargo.toml --locked --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          cargo audit --file native/windows-managed-process-helper/Cargo.lock --deny warnings
          cargo deny --manifest-path native/windows-managed-process-helper/Cargo.toml --config native/windows-managed-process-helper/deny.toml --locked check
          npm run check:windows-helper-reproducibility
          $env:PI_WINDOWS_HELPER_HANDLE_LOOPS = "100"
          npm run test:windows-managed-helper
          npm run test:managed-process-workflows
          $env:PI_MANAGED_FLOOD_DURATION_MS = "60000"
          $env:PI_MANAGED_FLOOD_PROCESSES = "8"
          $env:PI_MANAGED_FLOOD_STREAMS = "both"
          npm run test:managed-process-flood

      - name: Run unit and handler tests
        run: npm test

      - name: Run cross-platform quality checks (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          npm run format:check
          npm run lint
          npm run typecheck
          npm run check:dependencies
          npm run check:contract
          npm run check:pi-compat
          npm run check:toolchain-contract
          npm run check:toolchain-catalog
          npm run check:browser-i18n

  windows-frameworks:
    name: Windows managed framework acceptance
    runs-on: windows-2025
    timeout-minutes: 35
    env:
      CI: "1"
      NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: "1"
      STORYBOOK_DISABLE_TELEMETRY: "1"
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Set up pinned Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@v5
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: "21"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install pinned Rust toolchain
        run: rustup toolchain install 1.96.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --profile minimal --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc

      - name: Build authoritative Windows helper
        run: npm run check:windows-helper-reproducibility

      - name: Prepare pinned framework fixtures
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $nodeRoot = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "framework-node-root"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $nodeRoot -Force | Out-Null
          Push-Location $nodeRoot
          try {
            npm init -y | Out-Null
            npm install --save-exact --no-audit --no-fund next@16.3.2 react@19.2.4 react-dom@19.2.4 storybook@10.5.10 @storybook/react-vite@10.5.10 vite@6.4.3 typescript@5.9.3
          } finally {
            Pop-Location
          }
          $springZip = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "spring-boot-4.1.1-fixture.zip"
          $springUrl = "https://start.spring.io/starter.zip?type=maven-project&language=java&bootVersion=4.1.1&baseDir=spring-boot-4.1.1-fixture&groupId=com.example&artifactId=fixture&name=SpringFixture&packageName=com.example.fixture&packaging=jar&javaVersion=21&dependencies=web"
          curl.exe --fail --location --retry 3 --output $springZip $springUrl
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Spring Initializr download exited $LASTEXITCODE" }
          Expand-Archive -LiteralPath $springZip -DestinationPath $env:RUNNER_TEMP
          $springRoot = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "spring-boot-4.1.1-fixture"
          if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $springRoot "mvnw.cmd"))) { throw "Spring wrapper is missing" }
          "PI_FRAMEWORK_NODE_ROOT=$nodeRoot" >> $env:GITHUB_ENV
          "PI_SPRING_BOOT_FIXTURE=$springRoot" >> $env:GITHUB_ENV
          "PI_JAVA_EXECUTABLE=$((Get-Command java).Source)" >> $env:GITHUB_ENV
          "PI_MAVEN_USER_HOME=$(Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'maven-user-home-3.9.16')" >> $env:GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Run real managed framework matrix
        run: npm run test:managed-process-frameworks

  quality:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install pinned Rust toolchain (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: rustup toolchain install 1.96.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc --profile minimal --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc

      - name: Install Electron binary
        run: npx install-electron --no

      - name: Prepare verified bundled search tools
        run: npm run prepare:bundled-tools -- --target linux-x64

      - name: Configure Electron sandbox
        run: |
          sudo chown root:root node_modules/electron/dist/chrome-sandbox
          sudo chmod 4755 node_modules/electron/dist/chrome-sandbox

      - name: Run full verification
        run: xvfb-run --auto-servernum npm run verify

  package:
    name: ${{ matrix.name }}
    if: github.ref_type != 'tag'
    needs: [quality, test-platforms, windows-frameworks]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: macOS arm64
            runner: macos-15
            platform: mac
            targets: dmg zip
            arch: arm64
            tool_target: darwin-arm64
            artifact: pi-desktop-macos-arm64
          - name: macOS Intel x64
            runner: macos-15-intel
            platform: mac
            targets: dmg zip
            arch: x64
            tool_target: darwin-x64
            artifact: pi-desktop-macos-x64
          - name: Windows x64
            runner: windows-2025
            platform: win
            targets: nsis
            arch: x64
            tool_target: win32-x64
            artifact: pi-desktop-windows-x64
          - name: Linux x64
            runner: ubuntu-24.04
            platform: linux
            targets: AppImage
            arch: x64
            tool_target: linux-x64
            artifact: pi-desktop-linux-x64
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 35
    env:
      CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY: "false"
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install Electron runtime for Windows acceptance
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'

  release-contract:
    name: Validate release contract
    if: github.ref_type == 'tag' && startsWith(github.ref_name, 'v')
    needs: [quality, test-platforms, windows-frameworks]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: Verify tag and package versions
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_commit="$(git rev-parse "${GITHUB_SHA}^{commit}")"
          git fetch --no-tags origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main
          if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$release_commit" origin/main; then
            echo "Release tag must point to a commit contained in main" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

          node <<'NODE'
          const packageJson = require("./package.json");
          const packageLock = require("./package-lock.json");

          if (!/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/.test(packageJson.version)) {
            throw new Error(
              `Stable release versions must use x.y.z without a prerelease suffix: ${packageJson.version}`,
            );
          }

          const expectedTag = `v${packageJson.version}`;
          const versions = [
            ["package-lock.json.version", packageLock.version],
            [
              'package-lock.json.packages[""].version',
              packageLock.packages?.[""]?.version,
            ],
          ];

          for (const [source, version] of versions) {
            if (version !== packageJson.version) {
              throw new Error(
                `${source} (${String(version)}) does not match package.json (${packageJson.version})`,
              );
            }
          }

          if (process.env.GITHUB_REF_NAME !== expectedTag) {
            throw new Error(
              `Release tag ${process.env.GITHUB_REF_NAME} must exactly match ${expectedTag}`,
            );
          }

          console.log(`Validated release ${expectedTag}`);
          NODE

      - name: Refuse an existing public release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if is_draft="$(gh release view "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --json isDraft --jq '.isDraft' 2>/dev/null)"; then
            if [ "$is_draft" != "true" ]; then
              echo "Release $GITHUB_REF_NAME is already public; published assets are immutable" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

      - name: Verify managed runtime catalog against upstream releases
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: npm run check:toolchain-catalog:upstream

  release-macos:
    name: Sign and notarize macOS
    if: github.ref_type == 'tag' && startsWith(github.ref_name, 'v')
    needs: [release-contract]
    runs-on: macos-15
    timeout-minutes: 90
    environment:
      name: release
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build, sign, and notarize macOS
        env:
          CSC_LINK: ${{ secrets.MAC_CSC_LINK }}
          CSC_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MAC_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_ID }}
          APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD }}
          APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}
        run: npm run dist:mac:notarized -- --arm64 --x64

      - name: Verify both signed and notarized apps
        env:
          APPLE_TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_TEAM_ID }}
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          find_app_for_arch() {
            local expected_arch="$1"
            local app binary
            while IFS= read -r -d '' app; do
              binary="$app/Contents/MacOS/Pi Agent Desktop"
              if [ -f "$binary" ] && lipo -archs "$binary" | grep -qw "$expected_arch"; then
                printf '%s\n' "$app"
                return 0
              fi
            done < <(find dist -maxdepth 3 -type d -name 'Pi Agent Desktop.app' -print0)
            return 1
          }

          verify_app() {
            local app="$1"
            local expected_arch="$2"
            local renderer="$app/Contents/Frameworks/Pi Agent Desktop Helper (Renderer).app"
            local entitlements

            echo "Verifying $expected_arch app: $app"
            codesign --verify --deep --strict --verbose=2 "$app"
            xcrun stapler validate "$app"
            spctl --assess --type execute --verbose=4 "$app"
            codesign -dv --verbose=4 "$app" 2>&1 | grep -Fq "TeamIdentifier=$APPLE_TEAM_ID"
            codesign -dv --verbose=4 "$app" 2>&1 | grep -Fq "Authority=Developer ID Application:"
            entitlements="$(codesign -d --entitlements - "$renderer" 2>&1)"
            grep -q 'com.apple.security.cs.allow-jit' <<<"$entitlements"
          }

          arm64_app="$(find_app_for_arch arm64)"
          x64_app="$(find_app_for_arch x86_64)"
          verify_app "$arm64_app" arm64
          verify_app "$x64_app" x86_64

      - name: Verify packaged macOS update configuration
        shell: bash
        run: |
          node <<'NODE'
          const fs = require("node:fs");
          const path = require("node:path");

          function findUpdateConfigs(directory, matches = []) {
            for (const entry of fs.readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true })) {
              const entryPath = path.join(directory, entry.name);
              if (entry.isDirectory()) {
                findUpdateConfigs(entryPath, matches);
              } else if (
                entry.isFile() &&
                entry.name === "app-update.yml" &&
                entryPath
                  .split(path.sep)
                  .join("/")
                  .endsWith(".app/Contents/Resources/app-update.yml")
              ) {
                matches.push(entryPath);
              }
            }
            return matches;
          }

          function readScalar(document, key) {
            const match = document.match(
              new RegExp(`^\\s*${key}\\s*:\\s*([^#\\r\\n]+)`, "mi"),
            );
            if (!match) {
              throw new Error(`Missing ${key}`);
            }

            const value = match[1].trim();
            if (
              (value.startsWith('"') && value.endsWith('"')) ||
              (value.startsWith("'") && value.endsWith("'"))
            ) {
              return value.slice(1, -1);
            }
            return value;
          }

          function verifyUpdateConfig(file) {
            const document = fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8");
            const [expectedOwner, expectedRepo] =
              process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY.split("/");
            const expected = {
              provider: "github",
              owner: expectedOwner,
              repo: expectedRepo,
            };

            for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(expected)) {
              const actual = readScalar(document, key);
              if (actual !== value) {
                throw new Error(
                  `${file}: ${key} does not match the expected release repository`,
                );
              }
            }

            const forbidden = [
              [
                "feed override field",
                /^\s*(?:channel|host|protocol|requestHeaders|url)\s*:/im,
              ],
              [
                "credential field",
                /^\s*(?:auth(?:orization)?|headers?|password|passphrase|private[-_]?token|secret|token|(?:api|access)[-_]?key|(?:gh|github)[-_]?token)\s*:/im,
              ],
              [
                "credential-bearing URL",
                /https?:\/\/[^/\s:@]+:[^@\s/]+@/i,
              ],
              [
                "authorization value",
                /\b(?:Basic|Bearer)\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/_.=-]{8,}/i,
              ],
              [
                "GitHub token",
                /\b(?:gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,})\b/i,
              ],
            ];

            for (const [label, pattern] of forbidden) {
              if (pattern.test(document)) {
                throw new Error(`${file}: contains a forbidden ${label}`);
              }
            }

            console.log(`Validated ${file}`);
          }

          const configs = findUpdateConfigs("dist").sort();
          if (configs.length !== 2) {
            throw new Error(
              `Expected two packaged macOS app-update.yml files, found ${configs.length}`,
            );
          }
          configs.forEach(verifyUpdateConfig);
          NODE

      - name: Verify macOS release artifacts and metadata
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version="$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")"

          for file in \
            "dist/Pi-Agent-Desktop-${version}-arm64.dmg" \
            "dist/Pi-Agent-Desktop-${version}-arm64.zip" \
            "dist/Pi-Agent-Desktop-${version}-x64.dmg" \
            "dist/Pi-Agent-Desktop-${version}-x64.zip" \
            "dist/latest-mac.yml"; do
            test -s "$file"
          done

          node scripts/verify-update-metadata.mjs \
            dist/latest-mac.yml \
            "$version" \
            "dist/Pi-Agent-Desktop-${version}-arm64.dmg" \
            "dist/Pi-Agent-Desktop-${version}-arm64.zip" \
            "dist/Pi-Agent-Desktop-${version}-x64.dmg" \
            "dist/Pi-Agent-Desktop-${version}-x64.zip"

      - name: Run packaged toolchain E2E for macOS arm64
        run: npm run check:packaged-toolchains -- darwin-arm64

      - name: Upload signed and notarized macOS artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: pi-desktop-macos-release
          path: |
            dist/*.dmg
            dist/*.zip
            dist/*.blockmap
            dist/latest-mac.yml
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:

        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
